While demonstrating acid-base reactions, Ms. Rajnish, a science teacher added sodium oxide to HCl until it was in excess. Which of the following graphs correctly represents the change in pH?

(Each option is a graph of pH on the y-axis versus mass of \(\text{Na}_2\text{O}\) added on the x-axis.)

options.label: A
options.text: pH starts low (acidic), rises and curves upward to about 14, then plateaus high

options.label: B
options.text: pH starts high (about 14) and falls, plateauing around 5

options.label: C
options.text: pH rises linearly from near 0 up to 7, then stays flat at 7

options.label: D
options.text: pH starts high (about 14) and falls, plateauing around 7

text:
While demonstrating acid-base reactions, a science teacher added sodium oxide (\(\text{Na}_2\text{O}\)) to hydrochloric acid until the base was in excess. Which of the following graphs of pH versus mass of \(\text{Na}_2\text{O}\) added correctly represents the change in pH?

The figure shows four graphs of pH (y-axis, marked 0, 7, 14) against mass of \(\text{Na}_2\text{O}\) added (x-axis):
(a) pH rises from near 0, levelling off near 14.
(b) pH falls from near 14 down to a low value.
(c) pH rises from near 0 and levels off at 7.
(d) pH falls from near 14 and levels off at 7.

options.label: A
options.text: Graph (a) — pH rises from near 0 and levels off near 14

options.label: B
options.text: Graph (b) — pH falls from near 14 to a low value

options.label: C
options.text: Graph (c) — pH rises from near 0 and levels off at 7

options.label: D
options.text: Graph (d) — pH falls from near 14 and levels off at 7

text: A parachutist jumps off a plane and opens the parachute at time \(t_1\). He eventually reaches a steady speed and finally hits the floor at time \(t_2\). Which of the following speed-time graphs best shows the parachutist's descent?

options.label: A
options.text: Speed rises to a peak at \(t_1\), then decreases gradually and levels off to a constant (terminal) speed until \(t_2\)

options.label: B
options.text: Speed starts at a maximum at t = 0 and decreases steadily to zero at \(t_2\)

options.label: C
options.text: Speed starts at a maximum, stays high until \(t_1\), then drops sharply to a low constant value until \(t_2\)

options.label: D
options.text: Speed rises linearly to a peak at \(t_1\), then drops almost instantly to a low constant value until \(t_2\)

text:
Parallel rays from a distant tree are incident on a convex lens and form an image on the screen. The diagram correctly showing the image of the tree on the screen is:

A) Parallel rays pass through the convex lens and converge to a single point that lies exactly on the screen (the screen is placed at the focal plane, so a sharp point image of the distant tree falls on the screen).
B) None of these.
C) Parallel rays converge through the convex lens, but the screen is placed before the rays meet (in front of the focal point), so the rays have not yet converged at the screen and a blurred, larger arrow is drawn on it.
D) Parallel rays converge through the convex lens to a point, but the screen is placed beyond the focal point (after the rays have crossed), so the image is not sharp on the screen.

options.label: A
options.text: Diagram A — rays converge to a point exactly on the screen at the focal plane (sharp point image).

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram C — screen placed before the focal point, rays not yet converged.

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram D — screen placed beyond the focal point, rays already crossed.

text:
Which of the following is the velocity - time graph of a moving particle on which net force is zero?

The four options are velocity (y-axis) versus time (x-axis) graphs:
A) a graph that is zero except for a single instantaneous vertical spike, i.e. an irregular, discontinuous line.
B) a straight line rising with a constant positive slope from the origin (velocity increasing uniformly with time).
C) a straight line falling with a constant negative slope down to zero (velocity decreasing uniformly with time).
D) a horizontal straight line at a constant non-zero velocity (velocity unchanging with time).

options.label: A
options.text: Graph A (an instantaneous vertical spike, otherwise zero)

options.label: B
options.text: Graph B (a straight line of constant positive slope — velocity increasing)

options.label: C
options.text: Graph C (a straight line of constant negative slope — velocity decreasing)

options.label: D
options.text: Graph D (a horizontal line at constant velocity)

A prism ABC (with BC as base) is placed in different orientations. A narrow beam of white light is incident on the prism as shown in the figures (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv). In which of the following cases, after dispersion, the third colour from the top corresponds to the colour of the sky?

(Figure (i): upright prism, apex A at top, base BC horizontal at the bottom, beam on the left face. Figure (ii): inverted prism, apex A at the bottom, base BC horizontal at the top, beam on the left face. Figure (iii): prism with apex A on the left, base BC vertical on the right, beam on the upper face. Figure (iv): prism with apex A on the right, base BC vertical on the left, beam on the left face.)
